OCR_Text: यथा दृष्टि तथा सृष्टि।
Translation: As is the gaze, so is the creation.
Explanation: The way a person looks at the world determines how the world appears to them. Your perception shapes your reality.
Keywords: Yatha Drishti Tatha Srishti, Perception, Reality, Subjective experience, Vision, Consciousness

OCR_Text: सप्तमी दिवाकरः कालमुद्भवं न खड्गेन साऽशुभं च निर्मलं रैशीरोटसुषामले हारमर्च रेवतयो वरे रूऽडा मणिं यादि येऽकुऽऽऽले कट कानि च २८ अर्थवेऽत याऽमुभे के शरन्सर्वैः बाऽषु २९ रोविमलोलतहुः ग्रेयक मञ्चुत्तमे २५ अंगुलीयक रत्नानि समस्तास्वनुलीय च १ विश्वकर्मट्दोत सैपर मे चातिनिर्मले २६
Translation: The sun, the creator of time on the seventh day, [is cut] not by a sword. That which is inauspicious and pure—adorn the necklace with the moon-bright nectar of the Raishirota. O you best of Revatas, mounted upon the jewel, who go to the unblemished shores! And the armlets, and the Atharva Veda, and both of those hair-anointings for all—the brilliant gems on the fingers, and upon all the rings, O Vishvakarman, bestow them upon me in this supreme and immaculate state!
Explanation: The speaker addresses Vishvakarman and asks for various items to be bestowed upon them in a supreme and immaculate state. These requested items include a necklace adorned with nectar, armlets, the Atharva Veda, hair-anointings, and brilliant gems for the fingers and rings.
Keywords: Divakara, Vishvakarman, Atharva Veda, Ratna, Surya, Saptami

OCR_Text: भी०स० श्रीगणेशायनमः॥ जनमेजयउवाच॥ शरत् त्यत्रैयानस्तुभारतानोपितामहः॥कथमुस्वरएवादे हंकंचियोगमधारातयन्॥१॥वैशंपायनउवाच॥शृणु बापहितोराजन्सुचिर्भृत्वासमाहितः॥ भीष्मसुकु रुशईलदेहोत्सर्गसमाश्रयत् २ निर्वधमानेवथ मेउत्तरेवेदिवाकरे समाविशघरात्मानमात्मन्येव समाहितः ३ शुक्लपसस्यचाष्टम्यामाघमासस्यपा शिव
Translation: Śrī Gaṇeśāya namaḥ. Janamejaya spoke: "O grandfather, when the great war of the Bhāratas had ended, how did he cast off his body, and what yoga did he practice?"   Vaiśampāyana spoke: "Listen, O king, having purified yourself and remaining fully focused, hear how Bhīṣma, the scion of Kuru, resorted to the relinquishment of his body. When the sun had begun its northward course (Uttarāyaṇa), he absorbed his earthly soul into the supreme Self alone, with a focused mind, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha."
Explanation: Janamejaya asks how Bhīṣma discarded his body and what yoga he practiced after the great war. Vaiśampāyana replies that Bhīṣma gave up his body with a focused mind when the sun began its northward course, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, by absorbing his earthly soul into the supreme Self.
Keywords: Janamejaya, Vaiśampāyana, Bhīṣma dehottsarga, Uttarāyaṇa, Māgha śukla aṣṭamī, Yoga-dhāraṇā

OCR_Text: सद्योविष्णुः पराद्ध्र्संर्व्वाश्चेतुद्देवुतः परिगृह्य
Translation: Instantly, Vishnu and all the gods, having captured the supreme goal, turned their consciousness toward it.
Explanation: Immediately, Vishnu and all the gods captured the supreme goal and focused their minds on it.
Keywords: Sadyovishnu, Vishnu, deities, supreme goal, consciousness, Parardhra

OCR_Text: बृहस्पतेष्ट्वा साम्ना ज्येनात्रिंचाम्मसा वितिमा म्य न ङ्मतातितद्बृहस्पतेरेवेनमेत सायुज्यं सतोकृतांगमयति ।२४। अथाह सम्राड्युम स्सोसम्राड्युमस्ता वितिनिवदितमेवेनमेत संतांदवेन्योनिवादयथ्यंमहावीर्र्योयोन्य ५२ वेचीथ्यंसुष्या कें कोमूर्तंगोपायतेयेवेेत ५१ दाहत्रिष्ट्वाआहत्रिदिदङ्गः ।२५। अथो जितीः जुहोतिवावाचयतिवायदिजुहोतिृदिवाच यतिसमान्एवंघुः ।२६ सद्वाचयति अनि रेकाक्षरेणप्राणमुदजयतमुजेषंप्रजापतिः सप्तदशाक्षरेणसप्तदशःस्ताममुदजयत्त मुज्जेषमिति्तद्युदेवतानिरेतादेवताउदज्
Translation: By the Sāman of Bṛhaspati, through water, [they invoke] "Atrin," thus. Truly, by that very [rite] belonging to Bṛhaspati, he leads him to union and identity with Him. Then the Samrāṭ says, "You are the Samrāṭ, you are the Samrāṭ,"—thus he indeed introduces him and makes him known to the deities: "Which hero knew the womb? Which one protected the body?"—thus he speaks, saying this in the Triṣṭubh meter, [for] the Triṣṭubh is strength. Then he offers the *jitī* oblations, or causes them to be recited. Whether he offers them or causes them to be recited, the result is the same. He causes them to be recited [because] Prajāpati conquered the vital breath with the one-syllabled [sound], and He conquered the seventeen-fold stoma with the seventeen-syllabled [meter], with the thought, "May I conquer!" Therefore, whatever deities [are invoked], these very deities he conquered.
Explanation: Using Bṛhaspati's Sāman and water, a ritual is performed to lead a person to union with Bṛhaspati. The Samrāṭ then speaks specific phrases in the Triṣṭubh meter to introduce and make the person known to the deities, as the Triṣṭubh meter represents strength. Finally, *jitī* oblations are either offered or recited because Prajāpati previously conquered the vital breath and the seventeen-fold stoma with corresponding syllables to achieve conquest over the deities.
Keywords: Bṛhaspati, Sāman, Samrāṭ, Triṣṭubh, jitī oblations, Prajāpati

OCR_Text: सर्वं कारणोद्भवमस्ति ।
Translation: Everything originates from a cause.
Explanation: Everything in existence comes from a cause. Nothing exists without a cause producing it.
Keywords: Sarva, Karyakaranabhava, Causality, Utpatti, Origin, Hetu

OCR_Text: श्रीः कृ०आ० सू० ७५२ ब्रह्ममित्रस्यवरुणस्यशर्मापस्यामुरुवीराअरिष्ठाः ॥ तिस्रोभू मीर्धारयंतीरुतद्यूंत्रीणिब्रताविद्येअंतरंयम् । ऋतेनादित्यमहि वोमहित्वंतदर्थ्यमन्वరుణमित्रचाह ॥ त्रीरोचनादिव्याधारयंत हिरण्ययाः शुचयोधार्तपूतः । असंज्रतोअनिमिषा अदब्धा उरुशंसारुजवेमर्त्याय ॥ त्वंविश्वेषाम्वरुणसिराजाचेदेवा असुर्येवमर्त्यः । शतन्नौरास्वप्नारदोविचक्षेपणामायूंषिषिधि तानिपूर्वाः ॥ नदशिएणविचिकैतेनसव्यानप्राचीनमादि त्पानोतपप्नुयाः । पाकाविद्सवोधीर्याविघुष्मानीतअभयं ज्योतिरैषाः ॥ योराजंभष्क्रतनिम्भोददात्युंयंवर्धयंतिपुष्ट् यश्चनित्याः । सरेवान्यातिप्रथमोश्थेनवसुधावाविद्ध्ये बुंम्रप्रासः ॥ सुचिरपःसुयवसाभद्रउपसेतिवृइवयाः सु वीरः । नकिष्ठंबंधंपतितोनदूराघआदित्यानांभवतिप्रणीतौ ॥
Translation: Shri!  May we attain the wide, heroic, and inviolable shelter of Mitra and Varuna. Three earths do they uphold, and three heavens; three are the divine laws that govern the inner spaces. By cosmic order (Ṛta), O Aditya, great is your majesty, and great is that supreme dominion which Mitra and Varuna maintain.  The three golden, luminous, and pure celestial realms they uphold, pure and purified by duty. Unconquered, sleepless, and unhurt, they grant abundant praise to the mortal.  You, O Varuna, are the king of all, of gods and of mortals alike. Grant us a hundred paths and dispel our sleeplessness; lengthen our lives, as you did for the ancients.  You do not fail to discern the right from the left, nor the ancient from the recent, nor do you wander from the path, O purifier. The ignorant man, the wise, the hero, and the eloquent all reach your fearless light.  That king who unfailingly bestows bountiful wealth upon the pious—he whose ever-growing prosperity is sustained—that wealthy man moves forward first with his chariot, knowing the earth and bestowing abundance.  Blessed with pure waters, good pasture, and auspicious fortune, growing ever wider, rich in heroes—no one falls into bondage, nor strays afar, when guided by the Adityas.
Explanation: The text prays to the deities Mitra and Varuna for shelter, stating that they uphold three earths, three heavens, and divine laws. It describes Varuna as the king of all gods and mortals, and asks him to grant long life, dispel sleeplessness, and provide safe paths. Finally, it states that those guided by the Adityas receive abundant wealth, good pastures, and freedom from bondage.
Keywords: Mitra-Varuna, Ṛta, Cosmic Order, Celestial Realms, Adityas, Divine Sovereignty

OCR_Text: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलििरभाषत ॥ १४ ॥
Translation: Then Dhananjaya, filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, bowed his head before the divine being and, with joined palms, spoke.
Explanation: Filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, Dhananjaya bowed his head to the divine being. Then, with his palms joined together, he spoke.
Keywords: Dhananjaya, Vismaya, Hrishtaroma, Pranama, Krita-anjali

OCR_Text: मउम्म्र्म्यचावस्व-न्यायचनमोनोदेयायचनदीप्पायच ३१ नमोऽज्येष्ठायचकनिष्ठाय चनमः पूर्वजायचापरजायचनमोमध्यमायचापगल्भायचनमो जघन्यायचबुध्ध्रायच नमः सोब्याय ॥ ३२ ॥ नमः सोब्याय चप्रतिशर्यायचनमोयाम्यायचक्षेम्प्पायचनमः श्लोक्या यचावसान्यायचनमऊर्ध्व्यायचषष्ठ्यायचनमोवन्त्याय ॥ ३३ ॥ नमोवन्त्यायचफक्षा यचनमः श्रवायचप्रतिश्रवायचनमः आशुषेणायचाशुरथायचनमः शूरवायचावनोदिने चनमोवर्मिने ॥ ३४ ॥ नमोवर्मिनेचकवचिनेचनमोवर्णिणेचवरूथिनेचनमः श्रुता यचश्रुतसेनायचनमोऽहुप्यायचाहनन्यायचनमो ध्र्ध्र्सवे ॥ ३५ ॥ नमो ध्र्ध्र्नवेचप्रम शायचनमोनिषङ्गिणेचिषुधिमतेचनमस्तीक्ष्णेषवेचायुधिनेचनमः स्वायुधायचसुध न्विनेच ॥ ३६ ॥ नमः सुत्याय ॥ नमः सुत्यायचपस्थ्यायचनमः काद्यायचनीप्पायचनमः
Translation: Salutation to the destroyer and to the protector; salutation to the giver of food and to the luminous one; salutation to the eldest and to the youngest; salutation to the first-born and to the later-born; salutation to the middle one and to the most capable; salutation to the lowest, to the wise one, and salutation to the auspicious one.   Salutation to the auspicious one and to the defender; salutation to the controller and to the bringer of security; salutation to the celebrated and to the final; salutation to the one directed upwards and to the sixth; salutation to the resident of the periphery.   Salutation to the resident of the periphery and to the protector; salutation to the auditor and to the echo; salutation to the leader of a swift army and to the master of a swift chariot; salutation to the brave one and to the giver of protection; salutation to the armored one.   Salutation to the armored one and to the mail-clad one; salutation to the one wearing a coat of mail and to the defender; salutation to the renowned one and to the leader of a renowned army; salutation to the destroyer of enemies and to the slayer; salutation to the bold one.   Salutation to the bold one and to the destroyer; salutation to the bearer of a sword and to the quiver-bearer; salutation to the one with sharp arrows and to the warrior; salutation to the one with excellent weapons and to the archer.   Salutation to the traveler and to the one by the path; salutation to the one in the water and to the one in the marsh; salutation to...
Explanation: This passage consists of a series of respectful greetings offered to various dual qualities, roles, and states of being, such as the destroyer and protector, the eldest and youngest, and the first-born and later-born. It continues by addressing different positions, physical locations, and martial attributes, including armed warriors, armor-wearers, chariot masters, and those found on paths, in water, or in marshes.
Keywords: Shatarudriya, Namaskara, Yajurveda, Vedic hymns, Rudra epithets

OCR_Text: सं. १ श्रीडुंढिराजाय नमः। गणपतये नमः। ॥ ॐ ॥ अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम्। होतारं रत्नधातमम्। अग्निः पूर्वेभिर्ऋषिभिरीड्यो नूननैरुत। स देवाँ एह वक्षति॥ अग्निना रयिमश्नवत पोषमेव दिवे दिवे। यशसं वीरवत्तमम्। अग्ने यं यज्ञमध्वरं विश्वतः परिभूरसि। स इद्देवेषु गच्छति। अग्निं होता कविं क्रतुं सत्यश्रिस्त्रश्रवस्तमम्। दिवो देवेभिरागमत्॥१॥ यदङ्ग दाशुषे त्वमग्ने भद्रं करिष्यसि। तवेत्तत् सत्यमंगिरः। उप त्वाग्ने दिवे दिवे दोषावस्तर्धिया वयम्। नमो भरंतमसिराजंतमध्वराणां गोपामृतस्य दीदिविं वर्धमानं स्वे दमे॥ सः पितेव सूनवेऽग्ने सूपायनो भव सचस्वा नः स्वस्तये॥२॥ वायवायाहि दर्शतेमे सोमा अरंकृताः। तेषां पाहि श्रुधी हवम्। वायव्या
Translation: Salutation to Sri Dundhiraja. Salutation to Ganesha. Om.   I praise Agni, the household priest of the sacrifice, the divine minister, the hotar priest, who bestows the greatest wealth. Agni, worthy of praise by ancient and modern seers, may he bring the gods here. Through Agni, one obtains wealth, day by day increasing, prosperous, and abounding in heroes. O Agni, whatever sacrifice and ritual you encompass on all sides, that truly reaches the gods. Agni the hotar, the wise poet, true in his works, possessing the most glorious fame, may he arrive with the gods.   Whatever auspicious deed you, O Agni, will do for the pious worshipper, that truth belongs to you alone, O Angiras. Day by day, O Agni, we approach you with our thoughts, O burner in the night, bringing homage to you who shine as king of sacrifices, guardian of the cosmic order, radiant in your own abode. O Agni, be easy of access to us, like a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being.   Come, O Vayu, for you are a welcome sight; these Soma juices have been prepared. Drink of them, hear our call.
Explanation: The text begins with salutations to Sri Dundhiraja and Ganesha, followed by praises to the fire god Agni as a priest, provider of wealth, and bringer of the gods to sacrifices. Worshippers offer homage to Agni, asking him to accept their prayers, protect the cosmic order, and be easily accessible to them like a father to his son. Finally, the passage calls upon Vayu to come and drink the prepared Soma juices after hearing the call.
Keywords: Rigveda, Agni, Vayu, Hotar, Yajna, Mantra

OCR_Text: श्रीः अं. १ श्रीः ॥ श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥ श्रीपुरुषोत्तमाय नमः ॥ श्रीकीर्तनादे- वनप्रयेनियम्यसंसारजागटाः उमादिभिषतेशेषेभजराम्सुहर स्तमः ॥ १ रागादिरेगान्स्तानावत्रकानशेषकायप्रस्तानेंशस न सैत्सकामोटारतिदानांज्ञानयोग्पर्वेवैद्यायनमोस्तुनसे ॥ २ ग्रथान्ग्राम्ग्रकामीयसप्यायंघाक्यास्यामः इत्यनर्सैइगग्रेया ग्राम्तर्पयः आयुष्कामायमानेनथमाथैसवसाधनम् आयुर््वे दोपदेशेषुविधेयःपरमादरः ब्रह्मासरतायुषोवेदेप्रजापतिः मग्नित्थान्माश्विनौतौमदसतातमोभिपटासिकाव्नीन् ने गिनर्वेशादिकास्तेतएपञ्चक्रवाणितेनिरै तभ्णतिविषयकीर्णोभ्यः प्रायःसारनरोसस्यः क्रियतेशेगय्टयेनानिसेतित प्रविहरतत्म् कायबालग्रहोधीगंशल्यदंष्ट्राजगग्रहम् ग्रष्ट्वैर्गानितस्याह चिकित्सानोत्रमेस्थितम् वायुःपित्तकफभेतिश्रयोदोषाःसमासतः ॥
Translation: Salutation.  Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Salutation to Lord Purushottama.   [Invocation and praise to the Supreme Lord/Deities for the removal of worldly bondage and ignorance, and for the attainment of knowledge and liberation.]  Now, we shall expound the chapter known as the "Desire for Longevity" (Āyushkāmīya). Therefore, those who desire longevity should apply the utmost respect to the teachings of Ayurveda (the science of life).   Brahman remembered this science of life (Ayurveda); from Him, Prajapati [learned it]; from Prajapati, the Ashvins [learned it]; and from them, [Indra, the lord of gods, learned it]. From them, Agnivesha and other [sages learned it]; and they [sub-divided it] into five branches.   [Considering that] people are generally afflicted by various subjects and possess short lifespans and weak intellects, [this concise essence] is composed for their easy comprehension.   [Ayurveda] comprises eight branches:  1. Internal Medicine (Kāya-chikitsā) 2. Pediatrics (Bāla-roga/Kaumāra-bhṛtya) 3. Psychiatry/Demonic Afflictions (Graha-chikitsā) 4. Treatment of Diseases above the Clavicle/ENT (Ūrdhvāṅga-chikitsā or Śālākya-tantra) 5. Surgery (Śalya-tantra) 6. Toxicology (Daṁṣṭrā-chikitsā or Agada-tantra) 7. Rejuvenation (Jarā-chikitsā or Rasāyana-tantra) 8. Aphrodisiacs (Vṛṣya-chikitsā or Vājīkaraṇa)  The humors (doshas), in brief, are three: Vata (Wind), Pitta (Bile), and Kapha (Phlegm).
Explanation: The text begins with salutations to deities and introduces the upcoming chapter called "Desire for Longevity," noting that the teachings of Ayurveda should be followed by those wanting a long life. It outlines the lineage of how Ayurveda was passed down from Brahman through various figures to sages who divided it into five branches. Finally, it lists the eight branches of Ayurveda and states that the three bodily humors are Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.
Keywords: Āyushkāmīya, Ayurveda, Aṣṭāṅga, Doṣa, Caraka Saṁhitā, Āyurveda-avataraṇa

OCR_Text: विकृताविकृतादेहैरेहैर्निनैव वर्त्तयेति चे नेषामिषोपिषाभ्यो रफोमधोर्धसंश्रयः वयोऽहरात्रिभुक्तानां तेतत्तमध्यादिकाः क्रु। मातृ तैर्भैवेहिषमन्तोऽगोमन्द्राग्निः समैः समः कोष्टः कुरोमरु इर्मेयोषाम्बस्थारैः समैरपि भुकोतवस्यैजन्मादौ विषेलो ववि घक्रिमेः तैस्तनिसःप्रकृतयोक्षीणमध्योन्नमः एथक समधात समस्तास्तथेशुनियादि तोषत्ता तज्ज्ञा तोलङ्गुलः शीतः नरः सप्त मूलानिलः पित्तेमसेरतीगोऽसेलनुविसेमसंस्दवम् त्रिग्धः शोतोगुरुमेदः स्थूलोरक्तः स्थिरः कफः सेसगर्मोत्रपातञ्च तद्द्वितयकोपतः रसास्रमांसमेदोस्थिमज्जाशुक्राणिधातव सप्तग्रह्यामलामुत्रशुक्रक्षेटाटयोपिच वृडिः समानैः सर्वेषां विमरेतैविपर्ययः रसाः स्वाद्लवणतिक्तोष्णकषायकाः बडूममाश्रितास्तेस्त्ययाएवैबल्नयादः तन्नाद्यमारुतं ज्ञेनि
Translation: If one should ask: "How should one live, keeping oneself unaffected amidst both altered and unaltered states of the body?"—the response is given: through the avoidance of such things [harmful items/influences] just as one avoids poison.   The syllable 'ra' combined with 'o', 'ma', 'dho', and 'rdha' belongs to the breath and upper channels. Regarding the stages of age, days, nights, and consumed food—these beginning with the middle ones constitute the state of *kru*.   Through mothers and them, those who are afflicted by poison, possessing a dull *mandrāgni* (digestive fire), and balanced by equals, have a balanced gastric fire (*koṣṭha*), [residing in] regions like Kuru and Maru.   By means of *ime*, *yoṣā*, *ambasthā*, and others, even when equal, the one whose birth is marked by *visela*, *vavi*, and the secretion of worms—their intrinsic natures (*prakṛti*) are such that their middle [portion] is emaciated, and their upper part is prominent. They are distinct, having balanced *dhātus* (tissues).   Likewise, [those characterized by] *śuniyādi*, *toṣattā*, *tajjñā*, *tolangula*, being cold—such a person [suffers from] the seven root-winds (or *mūlānila*). In bile and flesh, there is excessive *go*, *sela*, *nuvi*, and the accumulation of phlegm (*sema-saṁsdavam*).   Oily, cold, heavy, of fat, stout, red, steady—such is phlegm (*kapha*), along with heat, perspiration, urine, and feces. From the aggravation of that pair [doshas], the seven *dhātus* (tissues)—chyle (*rasa*), blood (*asṛk*), flesh (*māṁsa*), fat (*medas*), bone (*asthi*), marrow (*majjā*), and semen (*śukra*)—along with waste products (*mala*), urine, semen, and *kṣeṭa*, are maintained. Their increase is brought about by things that are similar, and their decrease by things that are opposite.   The tastes (*rasa*) are sweet (*svādu*), sour (*amla*), salty (*lavaṇa*), bitter (*tikta*), pungent (*uṣṇa/kaṭu*), and astringent (*kaṣāyaka*). Relying upon the stomach (*āmāśaya*), they are [known] thus; by them strength and weakness are [determined]. Among these, the first is understood to be *māruta* (wind).
Explanation: One should live by avoiding harmful influences just as one avoids poison to remain unaffected by changes in the body. The text lists various physical elements, bodily humors like phlegm and bile, the seven bodily tissues, and bodily wastes, noting that similar substances increase them while opposite substances decrease them. Finally, it identifies the six tastes—sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent—which reside in the stomach and determine strength and weakness, with the first being wind (*māruta*).
Keywords: Ayurvedic physiology, Dhatus, Doshas, Agni, Rasa tastes, Prakriti

OCR_Text: प्रायो लिङ्गादयः कफें कषायं च क्रमधुपित्तमतृकुर्वते श् मनैकोपने सवरिते द्रव्यमिति त्रिधा उष्णशीतगुणोत्कषींज्ञा २वीर्यैर्द्विधास्तनम् त्रिधाविपाकेद्रव्यस्वादुम्लकटुकात्मका गुरुमृदुहिमस्निग्थलक्ष्णोष्णस्थिराः गुणास्तत्त्र्सवि घराविंशतिस्त्रिर्विकपयैः कालाथेकर्मणां योगादीनमिर्थै त्रिमात्रकाः सम्यगेगसम्बवितेयेरोगपरोरोगैषेककारणम् रोगस्तन्दोषषवेषम्येरोघसाम्यमरोगता निजगतंत्रविभागेनतः अरोगाद्विधामताः तेषांकायमनेभेरुथिक्षानमपिद्विधा रजस्तममुम्तमसोदैह्यश्चरोषाउद्याहतो दर्शनस्पर्शनप्रश्रैः१ परीक्षेतवरोगिणाम् रोगेननिधानंप्रारूपलत्तणोपशयाप्ति भिः ममित्दप्रभेरेनरेशमाङ्गेरिहद्विधा ज्ञागलेवानिभद् यस्मार्वृप्तकफोत्पन्नै साधारणसममलेत्रिधाम्भदेशमारि
Translation: Generally, markers such as gender and others aggravate kapha and kashaya (astringent), while in due order pitta and vata are pacified. A substance is known in three ways according to pacification, provocation, or being unchanged. Potency (virya) is twofold (hot and cold) or threefold based on the predominance of qualities, and also threefold in vipaka (post-digestive effect), being sweet, sour, or pungent in nature. The qualities (gunas) are twenty, starting with heavy, soft, cold, unctuous, smooth, hot, and stable. Through the permutations of time, substance, action, and combinations, they become threefold. When properly applied, these are the causes of health; their imbalance is the cause of disease. Disease is the imbalance of the doshas, and the equilibrium of the doshas is health. Diseases are traditionally classified as endogenous (nija) and exogenous (agantuja). Treatment is also twofold: physical and mental. Rajas and tamas are the mental doshas. Examination of patients should be conducted by means of interrogation, observation, and palpation. Disease is understood through its origin, premonitory symptoms, actual symptoms, and the attainment of relief through therapeutic measures. Knowledge is twofold by nature. Because it arises from vitiated kapha and other doshas, the region of water is characterized by common and balanced impurities in a threefold manner.
Explanation: This passage explains the effects of substances on bodily doshas, the properties of potency and qualities, and how balance defines health while imbalance causes disease. Diseases are classified as endogenous or exogenous, with mental doshas identified as rajas and tamas, and patients are examined through interrogation, observation, and palpation. Finally, diseases are understood through their origin, symptoms, and relief, while treatment is divided into physical and mental methods.
Keywords: Tridosha, Virya, Vipaka, Guna, Roga, Agantuja

OCR_Text: ज्योतिष ॥१९॥ ॥श्रीगणेशायनमः॥हरिःॐ॥पंचवत्सरमयंयुगाध्यक्षंप्रजापतिं। दिनर्व्यनमासांगंप्रणम्यशिरसाशुचिः॥१॥प्रणम्यशिरसाकालं भिवाद्यसरस्वतीं॥कालज्ञानंप्रवक्ष्यामिल्गधेसयमहात्मनः॥२॥ज्यो निषामयनकतंत्रप्रवक्ष्याभ्यनुपूर्वशः॥विप्राणांसमंतलोकेयज्ञका लार्थसिद्धये॥३॥निरेकंवादशर्द्वाद्विगुणंघृतसंज्ञिकं॥वष्याष ष्यायुतंक्ताभ्यांपर्वणांराशिरुच्यते॥४॥स्वराऽर्कमेकेसोमाकैर्यदासा केसवासवो॥स्यात्तदादियुतंमाघस्तपःशुक्लोदिनंत्यजः॥५॥१॥प्रपद्ये। ॥१॥
Translation: Jyotisha (Astronomy/Astrology) Salutation to Sri Ganesha. Harih Om. Having bowed my head in purity to the Lord of creatures (Prajapati), who presides over the five-year yuga, and whose limbs are the days, seasons, and months; having bowed my head to Time and paid homage to Sarasvati, I shall set forth the knowledge of time, according to the great sage Lagadha. I shall explain the sequential system of the movements of the heavenly bodies, which constitutes astronomy, for the brahmins, in order to ascertain the proper times for sacrifices throughout the world. [The text continues with astronomical and calendrical rules regarding lunar months, solar positions, tithis, and the beginning of the month of Magha.]
Explanation: The author begins by bowing to Ganesha, the Lord of creatures, Time, and Sarasvati before explaining the science of time and astronomy as taught by the sage Lagadha. This astronomical system of heavenly bodies is set forth for the brahmins so they can determine the correct times for performing sacrifices across the world.
Keywords: Vedanga Jyotisha, Lagadha, Kala-jnana, Yuga, Yajna-kala, Astronomy

OCR_Text: रु २ तेश्रविष्ठादौ सूर्याचंद्रमसावुदक॥ सापार्थेदक्षिणाऽर्कस्तुमाघः श्रावणे रा १ योः सदा॥१॥ धर्मर्द्धिरापः प्रस्रः क्षपौ सउदग ताौ॥ दक्षिणे तो विपर्य स्तौ षष्मुहूर्त्ययनेन तु॥२॥ द्विगुणंसप्तमं वाऽनूरयनाद्यैंत्रयोदश॥ चतु र्थंदश मंचैव द्वियुग्माद्यंबऊलेयतो॥३॥ वसुस्त्वष्टाभगोजश्च मित्रसर्पाश्विनोजलं॥ धाताकथ्श्वाध्यायनाश्वादू पंचैनभ खतुनाऽ॥ मांशासुरषकाः कार्याः पक्षा द्वादश चोद्गताः॥ एकादशगुणास्योनः भुक्लं द्वैर्दै इवायदि॥१०॥१२॥ कार्या भागा षका स्थाने कलाये काल विंशतिः॥
Translation: From the beginning of Shravishtha, the sun and moon turn northward. The southern course of the sun occurs in Magha. Thus, the solstices are always in Shravishtha and Magha.   Righteousness and water increase, water springs forth, and the nights become shorter when the course is northward; when it is southward, the reverse is true. The shift of the solstices takes place by sixty muhurtas (over the course of the year).  Twice the seventh, or thirteen from the beginning of the ayana (solstice); the fourth, tenth, and likewise from the double pair (twelfth), as known from the rule of the *bahula* (waning phase).  Vasu, Tvashtar, Bhaga, Aryaman, Mitra, Sarpa, Ashvinin, Jala (Varuna), Dhata, Kanthshva (Aryaman/Kuhuh), Adhyayana, Ashva, and the five stars of Abhijit...   Sixfold parts are to be made, and twelve fortnights have elapsed. Eleven multiplied and diminished... the bright fortnight... on the second or eighth day.   Parts should be established in the sixfold place, and twenty kalas for time.
Explanation: The text describes the movements of the sun and moon, stating that their northern course begins in Shravishtha and their southern course in Magha. During the northern course, nights become shorter while righteousness, water, and springs increase, with the reverse occurring during the southern course. It also lists specific constellations, numerical calculations for time, solstices, and fortnights, and instructions for dividing parts and measuring time using kalas.
Keywords: Jyotisha, Solstices, Ayana, Nakshatra, Shravishtha, Muhurta

OCR_Text: श्रीगणेशायनमः॥श्रीमद्गुरूयोनमः॥यंदेतत्सदपंकडंगएपतेयद्दीपरात्तंबु डंगेंडस्छअमरायणीमधुधियाशातिस्पृशंतिष्ठुः॥मेंझारहूंदत्ताचित्जमहात्वजो दियकिं चित्तदान्मंजुसजातशादृत्तिंविदधतीसत्तांडयेकालिकां॥१परंवरांतद्भगाना हियुक्तनविष्श्वरोयोदिविचंद्रयुक्तः॥अगारमाद्यांव्रिजहायमौजुरोषिपछंतरगो शिव्यैः॥२कुर्येरमलशास्त्रास्पवैचित्रंमु मनोहरं॥रामोदेवबिदोसैतेपुुरोक्षंब नेर्युथा॥३प्रादावजीएकुजदेवगंगाएम्पश्चाधिधिज्ञमपिदैयविंदावारिस्थैः॥स म्पूल्डेस्वस्सुरवक्रएविनिरंयार्थंप्रेश्छयर्मनजशास्त्राविदेनृपछेक्षणं॥रंधैयज्ञ मितोषिंदुःसमरंध्रूयंदुडामानमार्गेणविज्ञेयंक्रमास्थानचलक्ष्यवै॥परेरवेर्का जायतेरैवांश्चनूपैंजा़यतेतथा॥रेखाश्चन्यस्लमायोगेज्ञायतेसूपमेयच॥चतु स्थानाइहृक्रमपदनायंपंचमक्षिदं ततः षष्ठंरोक्तं तदुपरिमिंदं चाएम्मिांतं॥ द्वयोर्यो गेयोगेनवमदशमेज्ञानव्ययेक क्रमारज्ञेयंस्पष्टंतरतुनवमाद्द्द्योगनिषे॥१७विष्धै पदवेरंसंज्ञेशकलचेचहुरोदिते॥तयोर्येगेप्विदशंतदाद्वयोर्गजृनृपं ॥ प्रथ शफसकक्र्रमः॥ लस्थ्यानिऋबुदारखिलंततोकक्षुदरवारिजं॥उमातफरहोचैवो
Translation: Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Salutation to the venerable preceptor.   That which is the true essence, pure and radiant, which the wise attain through a tranquil intellect, touching the supreme peace; and that which brings forth a charming state of mind, I invoke that Goddess Kālikā to inspire this creation. (1)  Supreme is that fortune, and appropriate it is when the Lord of the universe, conjoined with the moon in the heavens, is in the primary abode, abandoning illusion, burning away obstacles through the disciples. (2)  One should compose this wondrous and enchanting expanse of pure treatises. Thus do Rāma and Devabinda make it manifest even though hidden. (3)  Having first honored the deities, the Ganges, and the lords of the quarters, and thereafter possessing supreme knowledge, one should present the true meaning of the treatise to the king for inspection, in accordance with the proper methods. (4)  That which is to be understood through the path of the measure of holes and defects (randhra), and likewise through the sequence of positions, is to be recognized precisely without missing the target. (5)  From the sun comes the dawn, and similarly from kings arises the majesty. Through the combination of lines and ciphers, the appropriate comparison is known. (6)  Here, the first place is the step of the sequence, the second is the eyes, then the third is stated, above that is the fourth, and thus ending at the limit. (7)  Through the combination of two in successive order, the ninth and tenth are to be known, and clearly, the prohibition of combination from the ninth onwards. (8)  By various designations of the parts and limbs when they are manifested, through their combination the tenth is produced, and then the union of the two creates the king. (9)  Thus is the sequence of the initial fruits: the first place is the timber-like, then the eye-born lotus-like, and similarly the... (10)
Explanation: The text begins with salutations to Lord Ganesha and the preceptor, followed by an invocation to Goddess Kālikā to inspire the creation of a wondrous treatise. It then outlines instructions for composing and presenting the work to a king, and describes various methods involving positions, lines, ciphers, and parts to understand measurements, sequences, and initial outcomes.
Keywords: Astrology, Jyotisha, Kālikā invocation, Planetary conjunction, House positions, Divinatory arts

OCR_Text: श्रीगणेशायनमः॥श्रीमद्गुरुभ्यो नमः॥ यदेतत्पदपङ्कजंगणपतेर्यद्द्यद्दरत्लोम्बु टंगंडस्खथ्मरायनीमधुधिया जातिस्पृशांतिक्षुः॥मंजीरच्छुरनिदत्ताचित्तजमहातेजो दियकिं चित्तदानमंजुलगतित्वांशद्वितीदधती सप्तांडयेकानलियां॥१परं वरंतयंगना दियुक्तनविध्यमेल्यो दिविविचंद्रसुत्तः॥अगारनाहांविजहायन्सौक्षरो तिपष्ठंतरगो शिव्यः॥२कुर्येरमलशास्त्रस्पवैचित्र्यंभुमनोहरं॥रामोदेवविदोंऽप्रौतैपुरोत्तृंयव नेर्युथा॥३प्रादावजीष्टकुलदेवगणांगएमप्पश्चाधिधित्रमपिदैवविदोंवारिष्टं॥स म्पफूलडो स्वस्तुरवकूएविनिरियाथंपैंशहयंरमलशास्त्रविदंनृपच्छेवर्ण॥रंध्रैधज मितोविदुः समरंध्रयंघूडः॥ग्राममार्गएविज्ञेयं क्रमास्थानचतुष्टथै॥परेरैयेकांख जायतेरेखा शून्येकांजायते तथा॥रे खासंचनगणाच्योगोजा यते शून्यमेय चान्दु स्खानाहई क्र्मपदनायंपंचमंछिंदं ततः षष्ठं प्रोक्त तदुपरिमंदं चाएममितां॥छ्योयो गेयोगेनवमदशमेज्ञानव्ययगे क्रमारतेयंस्पष्टंततु नवमाद्द्योगज निते॥विम्धे रवैवैंरसंज्ञे चशुकलेचतुरोदिते॥तयोयेगेप वदशंतदा छ्योयोगज नृपं॥ःप्रथ शकलकमः॥ तस्यप्षं कूडारिखिलं ततोकूडरवारिजं॥उमातफरहो चैवो
Translation: Salutation to Sri Ganesha. Salutation to the venerable preceptors.   1. That which is the lotus-foot of Ganapati, from which the fluid of rut trickles like honey, sought after by the swarm of bees—manifesting the sweet and graceful movement of anklets, possessing great splendor, and bearing a double share [of beauty]—may it bestow the supreme state.  2. [Verse 2 missing/corrupt in the traditional sense, but treating the context:] Abandoning the mundane household, the pure-lettered and accomplished disciple [proceeds to higher realms...].  3. May he create the charming and variegated science of Ramal (geomancy), as composed by the astrologer Ramadeva, just like the Yavanas before.  4. Having first worshipped the family deities and the host of divine beings, and subsequently the preceptors and the foremost astrologers... [the text proceeds into the technical mechanics of the Ramal divination system].  [Technical Geomantic Rules:] - Regarding the generation of lines and dots: from two lines a single line is produced, and from two zeros a zero is likewise produced. - From a line and a zero, a zero is produced; and from a zero and a line, a line is produced. - [Instructions regarding the four mother houses, daughters, nieces, and judges follow in traditional geomantic calculations]. - Through the combination of these, in the ninth and tenth houses, knowledge and expenditure are understood in sequence. From the combination of the ninth [and other houses], the clear result is born. - In the figures known as *Bayad*, *Naki*, *Sukh*, and *Chatur*, when they are produced... [the text concludes with the first section on the arrangement of figures such as *Kuda*, *Rikh*, and *Umatfarho*].
Explanation: The text begins with prayers and salutations to Ganesha, the preceptors, family deities, and astrologers, asking for the supreme state and the creation of the science of Ramal (geomancy) as composed by Ramadeva. It then details the technical rules of the geomantic divination system, explaining how lines and zeros combine to generate results across various houses, such as the ninth and tenth. Finally, it outlines the arrangement of specific geomantic figures like *Bayad*, *Naki*, *Kuda*, *Rikh*, and *Umatfarho*.
Keywords: Ramal Shastra, Geomancy, Ramadeva, Arabic astrology, Divination figures, Bayad Naki

OCR_Text: नः समाधिमावयति क्लेशांश्चप्रतनूकरोति प्रतनूकृतक्लेशांन् प्रसंख्यानाग्निनादग्धबीजकस्यानप्रसवधर्मिणः करिष्यति ते षांस्तनूकरणात्पुनः क्लेशैर्खरारामृष्टसत्पुरुषास्पतामात्रख्या तिः सूक्ष्मप्रज्ञासमात्ताधिकांराः प्रतिप्रसवयकरिष्यन्ति तेषां तनूकरणात्पुनः क्लेशैर अयपुनः क्लेशः के कियंतोवेति अधश्या सेत्रमुतरेषांप्रसुवृत्तनुविच्छिन्नोदाराणां ४ अत्रजविद्यासे त्रेप्रसवभूमिरुत्तरेषां अस्मितादीनां चतुविकाल्पानां प्रसुप्रत नुविच्छिन्नोदाराणां तत्रकामसुप्तिः चेतसिन्रक्तिमात्रप्रतिष्टा नाबीजभावोपगमः तत्रप्रबोधओलंबनेसेमुखीभावः
Translation: That which brings about meditative absorption (samādhi) and weakens afflictions (kleśas). Having thus rendered the afflictions weakened by the fire of discriminative discernment (prasaṁkhyāna)—such that their seed-nature is burned away and they are no longer subject to production—their mere manifestation, no longer touched by coarse afflictions, shines forth as subtle wisdom. Through their attenuation, those [modifications] ultimately resolve back into their source (pratiprasava).   [One might ask:] What and how numerous are these afflictions?  The answer is: From here downward, the subsequent ones are dormant, attenuated, severed, or active. Among these, the field of manifestation is for the subsequent ones—asmitā (egoism) and the others—which exist in four states: dormant, attenuated, severed, and active.   Among these, deep sleep (svapna/supti) is that state of the mind in which, resting purely in mere latency, it attains the condition of having its seeds intact. Awakening is the turning toward and facing an object of support.
Explanation: This text describes a process where meditative absorption weakens afflictions until their seeds are burned away by discriminative discernment, allowing subtle wisdom to shine forth before those mental modifications resolve back into their source. It explains that afflictions are either dormant, attenuated, severed, or active, with egoism and other subsequent afflictions appearing in these four states. Additionally, it defines deep sleep as a latent state where the mind's seeds remain intact, while awakening is the mind turning toward an object of support.
Keywords: samādhi, kleśa, prasaṁkhyāna, pratiprasava, asmitā, avidyā

OCR_Text: राम० ॥श्रीगणेशायनमः अथद्वितीयः पादः उद्विष्टः समाहितचित्तस्य योगः कथंमुत्थितचित्तोपियोगयुक्तः स्यादित्येतदुत्तरमारभ्यते तपस्वा ध्यायेस्वरप्रणिधाना निक्रियायोगः १ नार्तापस्विनीयोगःसिध्यति अनातृषिकर्मवासनां चित्राप्रकृष्टकष्टापिताविषयजाला चांसुद्धि र्नातरेणतपः संभेदमापद्यते रुतितपसमुपादानेन च चितप्रसा दनमनबाधमानमनेनासेव्य मितिमन्यतेस्वाध्यायः प्रणवादिप विच्चमंत्राणांजपः मोक्षशास्त्र्रोध्यायनेवा ईश्वरप्रणिधानेसर्व क्रियाणांपरमगुरावर्पणं तत्फलसंस्यासोवा सहिक्रियायोगः समाधिभावनाार्थः क्लेशतनूकरणार्थश्च २ सहिज्ञासेव्यमा शिक
Translation: Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Now begins the second pada (chapter).   Having explained the yoga of one whose mind is already concentrated, [the text] now begins to answer how yoga is attainable for one whose mind is distracted.   Austerity, study of sacred texts, and surrender to the supreme Lord constitute Kriya Yoga. Without austerity, yoga cannot succeed. The mind's impurity—consisting of unfulfilled desires, subtle impressions of past actions (vasanas), various intensely painful torments, and entanglement in worldly objects—cannot be completely destroyed without the smelting fire of austerity.   Therefore, through the practice of austerity, the mind becomes purified and untroubled; thus, it is considered worthy of being practiced.   "Study" (svadhyaya) means the repetition of purifying mantras such as Om, or the study of scriptures on liberation.   "Surrender to Isvara" (Ishvara pranidhana) means the dedication of all actions to the supreme Guru, or the renunciation of the fruits of actions.   This Kriya Yoga is [undertaken] for the purpose of cultivating Samadhi and for attenuating the afflictions (kleshas). Indeed, it is worthy of being practiced by the seeker.
Explanation: This passage explains that Kriya Yoga consists of austerity, the study of sacred texts, and surrender to the supreme Lord, which helps achieve concentration for a distracted mind. Austerity is essential because it acts like a smelting fire to destroy mental impurities, while study involves repeating mantras or reading liberation scriptures, and surrender means dedicating all actions or their fruits to the supreme Guru. Ultimately, this practice is undertaken to cultivate Samadhi and weaken the afflictions.
Keywords: Kriya Yoga, Tapas, Svadhyaya, Ishvara Pranidhana, Klesha, Samadhi

OCR_Text: यदादमथशब्दोविकारार्थमध्यवसायर्थ संपृचनइत्याह योमानुशासनशास्त्रमधिकृतमिति ननुछ्यारण्यार्धमानन्यायो गोपाधिकृतो मनुशास्त्रमित्येतदाह वेदितव्यमिति मुक्तंगुरुत्वाद्यमानन्यायोयोगइत्युक्त ममृतंयदिमयेणाशास्त्रेणकारोनयुतायूरसागोचरध्वयुता दकस्यव्यापारोन कर्मगोचर इतिकर्तृव्यापारविवक्षायायोगविषयत्यशास्त्रस्याधिकृतत्वंतत्वेदितव्यं शास्त्रव्यापारगोचरतयानुयोगएवा धिकृतइतिभाव अधिकारार्थस्यचाग्रिमस्यस्यार्थनीयमानोदकुनदक्रिनिबंधअशीमंगलौविनल्यल्पइजिमेतबे शब्द्संदेहनि क्तिमर्थसंदेहमुत्पन्यति योगःसमाधिः युञ्जसमाधावित्यस्मात् घुतृयंत्र समाधावर्थे नतु युजिर्योग इत्यस्मात्संयोगार्थइत्यर्थः। ननु योगा अनुशासनंशास्त्रमधिकृतंवेदितव्यम्। योगःसमाधिः। स चसमाधैर्योःमः। चित्तस्यधर्मः॥
Translation: When the expression "atha" is employed in the sense of modification (vikāra) and determination (adhyavasāya), it conveys conjunction, as declared by one who is competent in the authoritative treatise on instruction (anuśāsana-śāstra).   Now, one might object: just as the maxim of "the half-forest, half-field" applies to a cowherd, does it not apply here to the treatise of Manu? To this, it must be understood that just as the maxim regarding heaviness pertains to yoga, as has been stated—analogous to how water, when associated with a mechanism (yantra) or channel, engages in action, whereas on its own it is not the object of action—so too, when intending to express the agency of the doer, the competency of the authoritative treatise pertains to the domain of yoga. The underlying meaning is that the subject is indeed qualified precisely because it falls within the operational scope of the treatise.   Moreover, the import of competency regarding what follows—as implied by the terms concerning the embankment and regulation of water—might otherwise generate doubt regarding words and doubt regarding meaning.   "Yoga" means *samādhi* (meditative absorption). This is derived from the root *yuj* in the sense of *samādhi*, and not from the root *yuj* in the sense of mere conjunction (*saṁyoga*).   Now, the established text is understood to be: "Yoga is the authoritative treatise on instruction." Yoga is *samādhi*. And that *samādhi* is an attribute of the mind (*cittasya dharma*).
Explanation: The word "atha" conveys conjunction when used to mean modification and determination. The text clarifies that "yoga" means meditative absorption (*samādhi*), which comes from the root *yuj* meaning *samādhi* rather than mere conjunction. Finally, *samādhi* is stated to be an attribute of the mind.
Keywords: Atha, Vikāra, Adhyavasāya, Yoga, Samādhi, Cittasya dharma

OCR_Text: न तणादियोऽवस्थाकालोभेषजयोगकृत्। शोधने शमने च वेति समासाद्योषधं द्विधा। शरीरज्ञानारोधाणक्रमेणापरमोधमम्। वा पित्तविरेको वमने तथा तैलाभ्यञ्जनम्। घृतवैद्याक्ताशि-। वित्तमनोरोघोऽषधपरम्। भिषट्ड्याएरपस्यातारे वीपादा-। च्तषयं चिकित्सितस्थानिर्दिष्टेप्रते के चवश्चतुरङ्गमम्। दत्तस्ती-। यात्प्रशास्त्राथोत्सकमाशुविभिषक। वङ्कल्कल्पञ्चहृदयेमस्र-। मन्त्रयोगप्रमोषधम्। अत्ररक्तसुविदेत्तोमतिमान्न्यायचारके। प्राज्ञोयोगीभिषग्वेषात्तापकस्मात्त्विनापि। सर्वोषधत्तमे। रेदेनः पुंसोनितात्मनः। भ्रमम्भगोल्येतत्तथैषपोऽनुपद्र-। वः। मृतलन्हुरोधन्तप्रतिपारसेपति। गृहेषुञोलेषेकदो-। वभागोऽडाम्बुतः। शस्त्रादिसाधनः। रुछूसेकचरव्रतोगदः। शेषतारागवायाळःपथ्याभ्यासाहिपयये। अनपक्रमपवः।
Translation: Neither time, grass, nor any state constitutes the creator of medicinal combinations. Understanding medicine as twofold—consisting of purification and pacification—and following the sequence of bodily knowledge and obstruction, one distinguishes between the superior and inferior. Or, through the purging of bile, emesis, and likewise oil massage, ghee prescribed by physicians, and the nourishment of the eyes, the pacification of the mind and intellect is indeed the supreme medicine. The physician, expert in practice, radiant, and free from arrogance, administers treatment as designated in the medical treatises, observing the fourfold system. The wise physician, devoted to sacred texts and endowed with supreme skill, should swiftly administer the decoction, the paste, the formulation, and the heart-cleansing medicines along with mantra applications. Here, the intelligent practitioner, well-versed in blood-letting and guided by reason, a wise yogi and physician, eliminates the scorching fever even without other primary medicines. Through restraint of the senses and control of the self, one overcomes delusion and similar ailments without complications. The intelligent physician attends to the obstruction of the channels as taught in tradition, utilizing water mixed with milk, treatments involving instruments and other means, regimens of dry fomentation, bathing, vows, and the observance of proper diets, thereby averting the recurrence of disease without deviation.
Explanation: Time, grass, and bodily states do not create medicines, which are instead divided into purification and pacification, allowing a physician to distinguish between superior and inferior treatments. A skilled and humble physician follows medical texts to treat patients using methods such as purging, emesis, oil massage, prescribed ghee, eye nourishment, decoctions, pastes, and mantras. By relying on reason, sense restraint, traditional methods, and proper diets, the wise physician successfully cures fevers, removes bodily obstructions, and prevents diseases from returning.
Keywords: Shodhana, Shamana, Cikitsā, Bhaisajya, Caturangama, Rakta-visrāvaṇa

OCR_Text: ताभ्यां वा मनसः स्थितिं संपादयेत्॥३५॥ विषयवती वा प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना मन सः स्थितिं निबध्नाति॥ नासिकाग्रे धारयतो अस्यादिव्यगंधसंवित्सगंधप्रवृ त्तिः॥ जिह्वाग्रे दिव्यरससंवित्॥ तालुनि रूपसंवित्॥ जिह्वामध्ये दिव्यस्पर्शसं वित्॥ जिह्वामूले दिव्यशब्दसंवित्॥ इत्येताः प्रवृत्तय उत्पन्नाश्चित्तं स्थितौ निबध्नन्ति संशयं विधमन्ति॥ समाधिप्रज्ञायाश्च द्वारी भवन्तीति॥ एतेन च द्रादियग्रह मणिप्रदीपपरस्मादिषु प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना विषयवत्येव वेदितव्या॥ यद्यपि तत्र शास्त्रानुमानाचार्योपदेशैअवगतमर्थनं तं प्रज्ञोतमेव भवति एतेषां यथार्थाथप्रतिपादनसामर्थ्यं तथापियावदेकदेशोपिकारिणा स्वकरणासंवेद्यो भवति। तावत्स वै परोक्षमिव अपवर्गोदिषु सूक्ष्मार्थेषु न दृढां बुद्धिमुपादयति। तस्माच्छास्त्रानुमानाचार्योपदेशोयदलनाथे
Translation: Or, one may attain stability of the mind through those [exhaling and inhaling]. Or, a sensory-oriented mental activity, when arisen, binds the mind to stability. When one concentrates on the tip of the nose, there arises the perception of divine fragrance, which is the olfactory activity. At the tip of the tongue, the perception of divine taste. On the palate, the perception of form. In the middle of the tongue, the perception of divine touch. At the root of the tongue, the perception of divine sound. These activities, when arisen, bind the mind to stability, dispel doubt, and become gateways to the intuitive wisdom of Samadhi. By this same principle, it should be understood that sensory activities arising in regard to the sun, moon, planets, gems, the flame of a lamp, or other such objects are likewise sensory-oriented (*vishayavati*). Although in those cases the object is understood through scripture, inference, and the instruction of a teacher, and though it becomes fully illuminated by wisdom with the capacity to establish the true nature of things, yet, as long as it is not directly experienced by one's own faculties—even in part—so long, like something indirect, it fails to produce a firm conviction regarding subtle truths such as liberation. Therefore, scripture, inference, and the instruction of a teacher...
Explanation: The mind can achieve stability through exhaling and inhaling, or through sensory-oriented mental activities that arise when concentrating on specific body parts like the nose or tongue. These perceptions stabilize the mind, remove doubt, and lead to the intuitive wisdom of Samadhi, similar to sensory activities experienced with objects like the sun, moon, or gems. However, until these subtle truths are directly experienced by one's own faculties, knowledge gained solely from scriptures, inference, and teachers remains indirect and fails to produce firm conviction.
Keywords: Visayavati Pravrtti, Sensory-oriented mental activity, Cittasthiti, Mind stabilization, Divyajnana, Divine sensory perception

OCR_Text: पाचं· १३ मेवावश्यं कश्चिदर्थविशेषः प्रक्ष्षोकर्त्तव्यः। तत्र तदुपदिष्टार्थेकदेश प्रक्ष्षोते सति सर्वं सुसूक्ष्मविषयमप्यापवर्गानू प्रदीयते। एतदर्थमेवे दं चित्तपरिकर्म निर्दिश्यते। अनियतासु वृत्तिषु तद्विषयायां वशीकारसं ज्ञायामुपजातायां समर्थस्यात् तस्य तस्यार्थस्य प्रक्ष्षोकरणाय तथाच स तिश्रद्धावीर्यस्मृतिसमाधयोऽस्याप्रतिबन्धेन भविष्यंतीति॥ ३५॥ विशोका वा ज्योतिष्मती पुरुषस्य॥प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना मनसः स्थितिं निबधनीमनुव र्त्तते हृदयपुंडरीके धारयतोया बुद्धि संवित्। बुद्धि संहि भास्वरमाकाशक ल्प्यं॥तत्र स्थिति वैशारद्यात्तः प्रकृतिः सूर्येदुग्रहमणिप्रभारूपाकारेण वि कल्प्यते। तथा चास्मितायां समापन्ने चित्ते निस्तरंगमहोदधिकल्पं शांतुम नंतमस्मितामात्रं भवति। यत्रेदमूक्तं तमणुमात्रमात्मानमनुविद्यास्मीति राम १३
Translation: Certainly, a specific special object must be investigated. When a partial aspect of that taught object is investigated, the entire subject matter, even though extremely subtle, is revealed up to the state of liberation (apavarga). For this very purpose, this mental purification (cittaparikarma) is prescribed. When the fluctuating mental modifications (vrittis) are controlled and the designation of mastery (vashikara-samjna) regarding that object arises, he becomes capable of investigating this and that object. That being the case, faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration will arise for him without obstruction.   "Or [the meditation that is] sorrowless and luminous, [pertaining to] the Purusha." When such an activity arises, it secures the steadiness of the mind as one focuses it upon the lotus of the heart and perceives the intellect (buddhi). For the intellect indeed possesses a radiant, ether-like nature. There, through proficiency in stability, that very nature [of the intellect] is perceived in the forms of the brilliance of the sun, moon, planets, and jewels.   And when the mind is absorbed in the sense of 'I-ness' (asmita), it becomes tranquil, infinite, and akin to a motionless great ocean, consisting solely of 'I-ness' alone. Regarding this, it has been said: "Realizing that Self as no larger than an atom, one knows 'I am'."
Explanation: Investigating a specific object reveals even the most subtle subjects up to liberation, which is the purpose of mental purification. When the fluctuating mental activities are controlled and mastery is achieved, a person gains the ability to investigate objects and experiences unobstructed faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration. Additionally, a sorrowless and luminous meditation focused on the heart secures the steadiness of the mind by revealing the radiant nature of the intellect, eventually leading the mind to absorb into a tranquil, infinite state of pure 'I-ness'.
Keywords: cittaparikarma, vashikara-samjna, jyotishmati, asmita, apavarga

OCR_Text: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥ १६ ॥
Translation: I see You everywhere with infinite forms, with countless arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes. O Lord of the Universe, O Cosmic Form, I see neither Your end, nor Your middle, nor yet Your beginning.
Explanation: The speaker sees the Lord everywhere in infinite forms possessing countless arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes. The speaker also states that the Lord's end, middle, and beginning cannot be seen.
Keywords: Vishvarupa, Cosmic Form, Infinite Form, Ishvara, Omnipresence, Divine Vision

OCR_Text: न तानादिष्ववस्थावकालो भेषजयोऽग्नकृत्। शोधने शमने चेति समासाषोधनं द्विधा॥ शरीरज्ञाना रोगाणाम्क्रमेणापरमीक्षयम्। वस्तिर्विरिको वमने तथा तैलाभ्यञ्जनम्प्रैषौवेधैयत्तातर्शातित्तमनोरोषोषधेश्रयम्॥ भिषद्रज्याएप्पस्यातारोवीपाद। वत्तस्ये चिकिन्मितसनिहिंष्टप्रेतेकेचश्रत्रपुणंम्। दत्तोत्यो यांतृशास्वा योतस्कमांशुविभिषक। वड्डकल्पंउरुणणस॥ सन्त्रयोगप्रमोषधम्। अत्ररक्तसुविद्वेत्तो मतिमान्मार्गवारके। प्राज्ञो रोगीभिषग्वेषपात्तापकस्मात्वानापे सर्वौषधत्तमे॥ रेद्रेय्नः पुंसोनितात्मनः। भ्रमम्गल्पदेतत्रैपइणोउपद्वः। मृतल्पवृषरोगेनप्रतिपारसेपदि गृहेबनुग्लोयेकदो। वमागोडाव्लतः। शस्त्रादिसाधनः। रुच्छसँकरेखततो गदः। शेषक्तादाणवापाळः पथ्याम्भासाहिपयंये अत्रणक्रसप्पवः।
Translation: Neither time, place, nor state serves as a medicine to kindle the digestive fire. Purification and pacification—thus purification is twofold in summary.  Through knowledge of the body and of diseases, one should observe the ultimate sequence: enema, purgation, emetic, oil massage, prescription, piercing, and the refuge of soothing remedies for mental afflictions.  Physicians, medicines, attendants, and the patient—these are the four limbs of treatment. [The rest of the passage contains fragmented technical terms and corrupted archaisms regarding therapies, obstructions of bodily pathways, wise management of diseases, and dietary regimens.]
Explanation: Time, place, and state do not act as medicines to kindle digestion, and treatment is summarized as either purification or pacification. The proper sequence of care requires understanding the body and diseases to administer enemas, purgations, emetics, oil massages, prescriptions, piercings, and remedies for the mind. Finally, treatment relies on four essential limbs: the physician, the medicine, the attendants, and the patient.
Keywords: Purification, Pacification, Sodhana, Samana, Four limbs of treatment, Catuspada, Enema, Vasti

OCR_Text: पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसंघान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥ १५ ॥
Translation: O Lord, I see within your body all the gods and hosts of various living beings, as well as Creator Brahmā seated upon the lotus flower, all the sages, and the celestial serpents.
Explanation: The speaker looks inside the body of the Lord and sees all the gods, different groups of living beings, and Creator Brahmā sitting on a lotus. Also visible within the body are all the sages and the celestial serpents.
Keywords: Viśvarūpa, Cosmic Form, Divine Vision, Brahmā, Celestial Serpents, Bhagavad Gītā

OCR_Text: ॥श्रीरामाय नमः॥ उंकारं ऋषंभं मरुले निरा कारव्यापतते सचं रातस्मै श्रीगुरवेन म परमगुरवेनमः॥

OCR_Text: कासां हिक्कां ज्वरं पाण्डुं नियच्छति ॥ न तज्ज्वरे दिवास्वप्नं नाभ्यङ्गं मैथुनं स्त्रियः । क्रोधप्रयातवायां मर्कयार्यक्षविवर्ज्जयेत् ॥ नकषायं प्रसेसं च ज्वराणां तरुणज्वरे ॥ कषायनोकली भूजा दोषा जेतुं मुदुः स्वराः ॥ द्वोयावकाः कषायेण निम्मितो नरोज्वरै ॥ स्तनम्भनेन विषयचाने कुव्रीप्रवियभ्भुरं ॥ पाययेद्दोयहरणां मोहादा मज्नरेतुयः ॥ समुपं कृलसस्य जुकराप्रेरा पुरा मृसेतु ॥ मृदोज्वसेन यो दे हे प्रचने सुमल्य च ॥ पक्कदोयदिजा नीया ज्वरे देयं तथोषधा ॥ उत्रमं स्पएलं मा आत्रिभिश्चाक्षैश्च मद्यमे । जगन्या स्थापनानेन लेहिका थेयधेचु च ॥ औषधो बेभुकिपीतं चंतथोषधशे येत्रे ॥ नकरोतिंगदोयशं प्रकोप्रयत्न्यरोगा श्व औषधञ्च प्रूकारः ॥ तरुणज्वररूपः ॥ अथवातज्वरदिनीचिकित्सामाह ॥ स्निग्घोभस्थिरवृक्षपत्न्य लवरास्यादम्लतैलामवस्त्रानाभ्यञ्जनवस्त्रिमां समदिरा सच्चा हनोन्मर्दनैः स्नेहस्वेदिनम्यहनस्प रामस्नेहोपनाधिकं ॥ पानामहारविहारभैषजमिदं यानप्रशान्तिनयेत ॥ किराता का म्रतोदीष्यवृहतीद्वयगीक्षुरैः ॥ सस्थिरा करसीविश्वेः काथोवा तज्वरापहा ॥ पिप्पलीशारिवाद्वाक्षा शतपुष्वाहरे
Translation: Which cures cough, hiccup, fever, and pallor. Therefore, in acute fever, one should avoid daytime sleep, oil massage, sexual intercourse with women, anger, excessive exertion, and garlic. In the early stage of fever, one should also avoid astringent decoctions and excessive salivation. Astringents, because they are heavy, are difficult for the deranged bodily humors (doshas) to overcome. [...] One should administer [...] due to delusion, one suffering from fever [...]. A decoction made from [...] of Kiratatikta, Amruta (Guduchi), Dipyaka (Ajwain), Brihati-duya (two types of Brihati), Gokshura, Sasthira, Kantakari, and Vishva (Ginger) alleviates vata-fever. Pippali, Sariva, Draksha, Shatapushpa, and Haretakī...
Explanation: The text lists remedies that cure cough, hiccup, fever, and pallor, while specifying what to avoid in the early stages of fever, such as daytime sleep, oil massage, sexual intercourse, anger, excessive exertion, garlic, and astringent decoctions. It explains that astringents are hard for bodily humors to overcome because they are heavy. Finally, it outlines specific herbal decoctions and ingredients, including Kiratatikta, Guduchi, Ajwain, Brihati, Gokshura, Kantakari, Ginger, Pippali, Sariva, Draksha, Shatapushpa, and Haretaki, used to treat fevers and vata-fever.
Keywords: Tarunajvara, Vatajvara, Dosha, Chikitsa, Kiratatikta, Jvara chikitsa

OCR_Text: भिषक् रुक्षाय सगृहोरहन्या छागं न शंभुरं गसुषी शारिवाद्राक्षा शणपुष्या पुनर्नवा ॥ सगुरोयंबकाय तु वान ज्वरविनाशनं ॥ द्राक्षा गुड़ूचिका सम्यग्गायमानाः समरिचानिः क्वाथोस गुडिकाः थपि वेदान्ज्वरापहं ॥ साजाजी पिप्पलीमूलंभुङ्ग वैकराजृताः ॥ अभया वृद्धमृद्वीकातेहक्षओक्षरायोमिनंकुशिरारोपेवेरस्त्यक्षनाशेगुरूगाडताः ॥ कम्पन स्पन्द वैचेवअनिलज्वरनाशनं ॥ लवङ्गमृत्पल्क्षण्यमजार्जामूलनागरं ॥ पिप्पली कदुकंपागपरी नश्यनचूर्णाथयेः गूडेन मोदकं यस्य वा नज्वरविनाशनं ॥ लवंगादि ॥ वातिकज्वरे ॥ सद्यैघृतपानं शंसमे परं क्षीरं स शर्करं पापि घृतमिश्र विशेषतः ॥ घृतपानं ॥ वातज्वरस्य ॥ पित्तोपचारमाह ॥ तिक्तस्वाऽडुकपायशानीपवनच्छाया निशावी जनन्यो त्ताश्रूष्ट हवारिय श्रेजलै जलीगू डसंस्पशनं ॥ सर्पिः क्षीरविरेकं रुधिर स्त्रावप्रदेहार्दिकां पानाहारविहार भेभजनमि दं पिंतप्रशान्तिंनयेन ॥ दुरासभापर्यट कपप्रियंगु भूम्यानिसवासाक दुरो हिराणिनां ॥ जलैपिबेच्छर्करार्याचागढ तृष्णानपि ज्वरदार्हयुतः ॥ यक्रिकः ॥ यरोल यवानिः क्वाथोमधुनामधुरी हृतः ॥ तीव्रपित्तज्वरानम्नदीपानाम्नदाहनाशनं
Translation: Physician, for dry conditions, [give] goat meat with *saguropahan* [or appropriate meat soup], not sheep, along with *sasuṣī*, *śārivā*, grapes (*drākṣā*), *śaṇapuṣpī*, and *punarnavā*. For *saguroyambaka*, goat [meat/milk] destroys fever. Grapes and *guḍūcī* together, along with *gāyamānā* [or *gāyatrī*] and black pepper, prepared as a decoction or pills along with *vedan*, destroys fever. [Another formula:] *sājājī* (cumin), *pippalīmūla*, *bhṛṅga*, *vaikarājṛtā*, *abhayā*, *vṛddhamṛdvīkā*... [fragmentary verse on managing burning sensations, thirst, and Pitta fever through appropriate drinks, diet, and lifestyle, blood-letting, and purgation with medicated ghee and milk]. *Durālabhā*, *paryaṭaka*, *priyaṅgu*, *bhūmyāmalakī*, *vāsā*, *durohirāṇi* — these taken with water and sugar quench thirst and alleviate burning fever. [Heading:] Yava and yavānī decoction sweetened with honey destroys acute Pitta fever, thirst, and burning sensation.
Explanation: This text provides specific remedies and treatments for different types of fevers. It lists various herbal mixtures, meats, decoctions, pills, and dietary guidelines—such as consuming ghee and milk—to cure fevers caused by Vata and Pitta conditions, along with symptoms like tremors, burning sensations, and thirst.
Keywords: Vātajvara, Pittajvara, Bhiṣak, Kvātha, Modaka, Sarpirvirecana

OCR_Text: कीने दो विशेषतः सुवर्च्चिका॥ यवक्षारेण लघुः स्निग्धो मुष्णो वह्निदीपनः। निहंति कुष्ठ वातानंमेदो श्वासगलामयानां। पां प क इ श्री शि रु गु णाना मा रु शी रुहृदयानमायां। स्वर्ज्जिकाक्षारगुणाताः रसादिश्लेष्मगुल्महरः॥ सुवर्च्चिकास्वर्जिकाचक्षोः चक्षुष्यो व्याधिगुणातो जिनेः॥ अथसोदरागा॥ सोभागंष्टंकांशांश्चधतुज तुर्भा वकमुच्यते॥ टंकतांवहिरकंदुसकफरूदातपित्तकृत॥ सारद्वयं॥ सारत्रयं॥ स्वर्ज्जिकायावकंचैवसारद्वयमुदाहृतं॥ टंकंननषतंनतुसारत्रयमुदितं॥ मिलितंतत्त्र त्रयं गु कु रु रु दि डि शोया या रु म् म ह रत्येरं॥ सारष्टकं॥ पलाशवज्ञिशिखरिवि वि सार्कतिलनालजाः। यवजास्वर्जिकाचेति सारष्टकमुदाहृतं॥ सारत्रेतः त्रैः त्रिनातु तु स्या स्या त्कु गु डस श रः सः दष्टस्यैः॥ अथतुक्का क्का चुकं सहस्रवेधिस्वादुसा सा हस्त्रंशुक्रमित्यपि॥ शुक्रमत्यन्तमुष्णंचदापनं पाचुपरं॥ शूलगुल्मविबंधामवातशलेह लेष्म हरंरसः॥ वमितुर रु ज्ञास्यवेदस्यहरती ती दावहिमांसुहरतः॥ ११०
Translation: Potassium carbonate and specifically *suvarcikā* (natron/sodium carbonate): Yavakṣāra (potassium carbonate from barley) is light, unctuous, hot, and digestive; it destroys leprosy, vāta disorders, fat, dyspnea, and throat diseases. [It cures...] and heart ailments. The properties of *sarjikākṣāra* (sodium carbonate): it destroys fluid/lymph-related disorders, phlegm, and abdominal tumors (gulma). *Suvarcikā* and *sarjikā* are beneficial for the eyes and cure various diseases according to the experts.   Now, regarding *sodarāgā* (borax): Borax, tankana, and related substances are discussed. Tankana alleviates phlegm and vāta, while aggravating pitta.   The two essences (*sāra-dvaya*): *sarjikā* and *yavakṣāra* are declared to be the pair of essences (*sāra-dvaya*).   The three essences (*sāra-traya*): When tankana is added to the previous two, it is spoken of as the triad of essences (*sāra-traya*). Combined, that triad of three... destroys... [various ailments].   The eight essences (*sāra-aṣṭaka*): [The ashes of] palāśa, vahni (chitraka), śikhari (amaphalā/apāmārga), vi..., arka, and tilanāla (sesame stalks), along with yavakṣāra and sarjikā, are declared to be the eight essences (*sāra-aṣṭaka*).   Now, regarding *tukkācuka* (or *sukra/tankana* varieties): Sahasravedhi, svādu..., sahasra, also known as śukra. Śukra is extremely hot and digestive... It is a fluid/substance that destroys colic, abdominal tumors (gulma), constipation, rheumatism, phlegm-related ailments... it removes vomiting, pain in the mouth, bodily distress... removes fever and morbid flesh.
Explanation: The text lists various alkaline substances and minerals—such as potassium carbonate, sodium carbonate, borax, and plant ashes—along with their specific combinations called essences. Translation: Obeisance to Sri Ganesha. Translation: In the secret part of the hand, at the base of the thumb, leaving aside one finger's breadth, by means of piercing with ink, and then pressing downward repeatedly with the fingers, one should examine the pulsations of the subtle channels of the hand, according to the scriptures, tradition, and personal experience, for the attainment of well-being.  In the beginning, within the vital channels carrying the breath, which are blazing like fire, the intelligent practitioner should understand the condition of the pulse through disorders of phlegm.   In terms of its meaning: when wind (vata) is predominant, the pulse becomes clearly manifest at the base of the index finger; when bile (pitta) is predominant, it is in the middle finger; and when phlegm (kapha) is predominant, it is felt as a globule in the third (ring) finger. When both wind and phlegm are present, it is in the index and middle fingers. When bile is predominant, it is distinctly in the middle and ring fingers. When wind, pitta, and kapha are all present together across the three fingers, the three doshas are to be recognized as conjoined.  The pulse belonging to the wind current is fickle (chapala); the one carrying bile is steady (sthira); the one possessing phlegm is declared to be sluggish and heavy; and the one exhibiting all characteristics possesses speed. Due to phlegm, it is steady and slow; when mixed, it is observed through mixed signs. Thus, the expert should declare the prognostic outcome.
Explanation: To examine the pulse, a practitioner presses a specific spot near the base of the thumb on the hand to feel the subtle channels for well-being. The location and movement of the pulse indicate which bodily humors—wind, bile, or phlegm—are dominant or mixed. Each humor produces distinct physical characteristics in the pulse, allowing an expert to observe these signs and determine the condition.
Keywords: Nadi Pareeksha, Pulse diagnosis, Vata Pitta Kapha, Ayurveda sphurana, Marma nadi, Rogi pariksha

Explanation: This text describes a specific type of water that is prescribed by the wise to restore bodily equilibrium and cool agitated blood. Translation: Salutation to Lord Ganesha.   The embodied form of the Moon is mentally conceived through the recurrence of births; for the faithful and the knowers of the Self, it is the sacrificial rite; for those who perform sacrifices, it is the minister and the lord of the assembly. Establishing the sustenance, origin, and dissolution of the worlds as its abode, He who is renowned spoke thus: He who possesses a multitude of rays like the soul of the ten directions, the lamp of the world, shining brightly, is comprehended by the wise with sharp intellects. For those of keen understanding who desire to know the results of horoscopy, and who are endowed with unseen fortune, even the skilled in auspicious and efficient fields find their efforts broken in the great ocean of horoscopic science.   Therefore, I commence this treatise, which is varied, meaningful, rich in scriptural knowledge, and known by the wise. Some desire 'Hora' to be a modification of 'ahoratra' (day and night), derived from the acquisition of actions earned through the nature of the sun and the other planets. Thus, the series of the zodiacal signs (beginning with Aries) manifested in regular order corresponds to the bodily limbs: the head of the cosmic purusha is Aries, Taurus is the face, Gemini the chest, Cancer the heart, Leo the stomach, Virgo the hips, Libra the lower abdomen, Scorpio the genitals, Sagittarius the thighs, Capricorn the two knees, Aquarius the shanks, and Pisces the two feet.   The terms *rasi*, *kshetra*, *griha*, *riksha*, and *bha* are synonyms denoting the zodiacal signs. Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are fiery; Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn are earthy; Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius are airy; Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are watery.   The lords of the planets from the Sun onwards are the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn; and the preceptors of the gods are Saturn... [The text continues detailing the divisions of *navamsha*, *drekkana*, *hora*, *sapthamsha*, *dwadashamsha*, and *trishamsha* according to classical astrological principles].
Explanation: The text begins with a salutation to Lord Ganesha and an introduction to astrological science, noting that even the wise find it vast. It then explains that the zodiac signs correspond to different parts of the cosmic body, starting with Aries at the head and ending with Pisces at the feet.
